newsitem.title: BOSNIA: German, French ministers visit Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: German, French ministers visit Bosnia.

text.p: German and French defence ministers said on Monday the planned deployment of a Franco- German peacekeeping contingent to Bosnia marked a historic moment for Europe.

Germany's Volker Ruehe and his French counterpart Charles Millon flew to Sarajevo to check on preparations for the force, which will see the deployment of German combat units abroad for the first time since World War Two.
Ruehe said military cooperation between two former enemies carried important symbolism for peacekeeping efforts in the Balkans.
"You know the history of Germany and France and here you have a German-French unit and I think this stands for the future, for the 21st century," Ruehe told reporters.
"It shows what we have overcome in the past and I hope this will give some hope to the people here that one can overcome divisions and hatred."

Some 3,000 German soldiers, sailors and airmen will join the NATO-led stabilisation force in January to help enforce the peace agreement in former Yugoslavia, where memories of atrocities committed by Hitler's Nazis are still alive.

A German force of 2,000, part of a Franco-German brigade based in Germany, will move into Bosnia itself and will serve under French command in the southeast region around the town of Mostar, inside Moslem-Croat federation territory.
The deployment "shows Germany doesn't go on its own, but we do this together with the French and we do this under a NATO operation," Ruehe said.

At a press conference earlier, Millon said the Franco-German unit was a "significant sign for Europe, for Bosnia and for peace". The soldiers' mission was to "defend the peace and stabilise security", Millon said.
The two ministers later flew by helicopter to Mostar to meet French officers who will command the Franco-German task force.
Ruehe has said previously that a German chief-of-staff will be appointed to the NATO-led mission sometime next year to reflect the Bundeswehr's more prominent peacekeeping role.
NATO officers in Sarajevo have refused to comment about the post, currrently held by a British general.
Asked whether he still expected the post to go to a German, Ruehe said, "We have made arrangements with NATO and they mirror the strengths of the German troops.
An advance team of some 70 German officers is already in Sarajevo preparing for the arrival of the combat units.
The German troops will arrive with Fuchs armoured reconaissance vehicles equipped with 20 mm machine guns as well as armoured personnel carriers.
But the Germans, sensitive to stirring up memories of World War Two, will not be driving tanks in Bosnia.
Ruehe has led efforts to remove the taboo on German troops serving abroad, culminating in a vote by the German parliament this month approving the use of combat troops in the Balkans.
